overall: As of 01:00 ET, Atlanta is in overnight cooling mode with the current temp at 75.2°F and falling at -3.6°F/hr — well below what daytime heating will bring. Skies are broken (62% cloud cover) with a very humid airmass in place (dewpoint 71.6°F), which will sustain elevated overnight lows but also moderate the daytime peak through latent heat effects.
forecast_obs_notes: There is meaningful model disagreement: HRRR is bullish at 87.8°F, NWS text forecasts a high near 86°F, ECMWF sits at 83.8°F, and NBM is the coolest at 81.7°F — a 6°F spread that makes confident positioning difficult. max_temp_prediction: The weight of evidence — NWS text (86°F), HRRR (87.8°F), and the META distribution centered on 86-89°F — points to a daily high in the mid-to-upper 80s. The mostly sunny afternoon with only a slight (20%) chance of a late T-storm around 3-4pm should allow solid surface heating, but the high dewpoint and lingering morning cloud cover will act as a modest cap. Confidence is moderate-low given the 6°F inter-model spread and high entropy in the ensemble signals; best estimate is approximately 87°F, with meaningful uncertainty spanning roughly 84-90°F.
